summary: Almost all of the audience is on Instagram, where the Hindi videos get 100 to 1,400 views, while YouTube Shorts barely moves (most videos under 25 views). The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner, with about 1,900 total views and the most likes, shares and saves, followed by the street light video. Sample sizes are tiny and the videos are only a few days old, so treat these as early signals, not proof.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first explainers about a common sensor people meet in daily life (PIR motion sensor, street light sensor). The title opens with a surprising claim or a 'how does it know?' question ('Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!'), uses Hinglish with a thinking emoji, and promises one simple answer. Videos that tie a sensor to something viewers see every day get the shares and saves.
doMore: Pick everyday things people have seen (lights, doors, taps, ATMs) and explain the hidden sensor inside
Open with a bold, slightly shocking claim in the title, like the PIR 'doesn't see you' line
Post Instagram-first and keep Hindi narration, since English Arduino video got no IG views and few YT views
End with a prompt that invites saves or shares, such as 'Save this for your next project' or 'Send to a friend who wonders about this'
Reuse the PIR angle with a part 2 or a related myth-busting follow-up, then compare results
stopDoing: Generic title patterns that only ask a plain question (Smoke Detector, Smartwatch, IR Sensor) which got low shares and saves
Posting English-language videos or relying on YouTube Shorts for reach until you find a hook that works there
